analysis: The change touches only docs/architecture/inference.md, with no code, config or policy changes. The supplied units (head lines 2463-3230) are unchanged context. The patch excerpt shows the changed hunks: a date bump, a new cluster health-file paragraph near head line 3528, and a cluster runtime facts rewrite near head lines 5230+. Those hunks fall outside the supplied head text, so I could not examine their full content. I did not find a security regression in the visible text. The visible context describes existing controls: typed 400 rejection of unsupported reasoning effort before Jinja, media caps, fail-closed Prism and cluster checks, a local owner launch that accepts no peer-supplied environment, and encrypted-prefix-cache scope notes consistent with T-041/SEC-035. Nothing there weakens the TB-002, TB-003, TB-007 or TB-011 assumptions or the T-041 cache posture. The patch excerpt describes two behaviors I could not check against code. (1) DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE gives the service and its coordinator-paired part separate heartbeat files, with the supervisor's liveness guard accepting only the service's own PID. The PID check, file permissions and path trust are not in evidence. (2) Signed releases compute cluster runtime digests from the final app and register them as cluster_runtime, a trust-relevant admission approval. The registering code is outside this batch. Both are documentation claims, not verified code changes. The head text of those hunks was not supplied, so the next pass should check them if the corresponding source files are in the PR.
